name: WI-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+11 district with incumbent Scott Fitzgerald running and a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage
Challenger Andrew Beck has raised only about $15,000, with no outside spending on either side
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds at just 2-3%
No public polls or expert ratings show any competitive threat; wave years have not put this seat in play
model.rationale: An R+11 incumbent seat, Fitzgerald's ~$1.3 million war chest against Beck's ~$3,000, and markets near 97% Republican leave the challenger without a visible path. Even a favorable national environment only trims the expected margin toward the high teens rather than making the race competitive.
model.watch: Major outside spending on Beck's behalf or a scandal involving Fitzgerald would be the main developments that could narrow the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Fitzgerald, the Republican incumbent, seeks another term in a district that leans Republican by about 11 points and has historically voted GOP by even wider margins in actual elections. He enters the general election with roughly $1.3 million on hand after raising about $1.4 million. Democratic nominee Andrew Beck has reported raising only about $15,000, leaving him with little visible capacity to compete. No public polls or expert ratings target the race, and prediction markets put Democratic win chances at only a few percent.

The national political environment could be more favorable to Democrats than in recent cycles, but even strong wave years have not brought this seat close. Barring an unexpected development, Fitzgerald is positioned for a comfortable win, with the main open question being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
